time.title: After the Evacuation Fire
time.note: Retreating Confederates fire the warehouses on 2–3 April; some 35 blocks of the business district burn.

curated.name: Great Turning Basin, James River & Kanawha Canal
curated.note: The canal's Great Basin covered three blocks between Cary and Canal Streets, from 8th to 12th Street. Completed about 1800, and still drawn on the 1886 Sanborn map; later filled and used as a rail yard after the railroad took over the canal (the end date here is approximate). The James Center stands on the site.

curated.name: Burned district, Evacuation Fire of 3 April 1865
curated.note: Some 35 blocks burned as the Confederate government left the city, from 4th Street east to 16th Street and from the river north, in places, as far as Capitol Square. Drawn simplified: 4th to 16th Streets, from midway between Main and Franklin Streets to the river. The mills and warehouses along the canal burned with it.

curated.name: Libby Prison (warehouses, 1845–52; prison 1862–65)
curated.note: Three brick warehouses, each 110 × 44 ft and four storeys, on the east side of 20th Street between Cary and Dock. Used as a Confederate prison 1862–65; dismantled in 1889 and re-erected in Chicago. Footprint from the published dimensions, placed at the corner; not surveyed.

curated.name: Gallego Mills, the great mill of 1854
curated.note: Twelve storeys, 96 ft on Canal Street and 165 ft deep, at the southwest corner of 12th and Canal: by 1860 the largest building in Richmond and claimed as the largest flour mill in the world. Burned in the Evacuation Fire. Footprint from the published dimensions; position from the marker; height assumes about 3.3 m a storey.

curated.name: Lumpkin's Jail (slave-trading complex)
curated.note: The largest of Richmond's slave jails, in the slave-trading district of Shockoe Bottom: a two-and-a-half-storey brick building about 41 ft long, operated from the 1830s until 1865 and demolished by 1876. Its foundations were excavated in 2008 beside Main Street Station. Footprint approximate; position from the historical marker.

curated.name: Shockoe Creek (open stream)
curated.note: The creek ran open between present-day 15th and 16th Streets, dividing the town, until it was enclosed in a culvert in 1877. Course approximated as midway between the two streets.
